answers.referenceSolution: At each steady speed the fixed-gearing drive torque balances resistance. Air drag on the same rider and bicycle increases with relative air speed, while rolling and equivalent mechanical resistance are approximated unchanged. Consequently more drive torque and effective tangential pedal force are required. Static tire friction supplies adjustable traction, not a fixed resisting force. Greater power from faster pedaling alone does not prove greater force.
conventionsAndLimits: Same rider, bicycle, posture and gear; level road and still air; steady speeds rather than acceleration.
Effective pedal force is the torque-producing component, suitably averaged over a pedaling cycle.
Mechanical loss belongs in drive torque accounting, not as a fictitious extra external force.
No numeric drag law, coefficient or universal speed threshold.

wholeQuestionCoverage.referenceSolution: No streamlining is needed for the purpose of reducing air drag in the stipulated airless space, because there is no surrounding air. Other forces and mission, structure and thermal requirements remain possible.

wholeQuestionCoverage.case: exposed launch rocket and fairing in atmosphere
wholeQuestionCoverage.referenceSolution: Aerodynamic shaping for the intended incoming-flow direction is useful while crossing air because it can reduce drag and aerodynamic loads, subject to payload, strength, heating, stability and changing-flow constraints. This reason is stage-specific, not a rule for all flight.

conventionsAndLimits: Use the distinction already resolved in the approved prompt; do not alter or re-review it.
Do not extend the vacuum-only conclusion to atmospheric entry or re-entry.
Re-entry heat protection can require a blunt shape; not all missions or flight phases require a pointed shape.

answers.referenceSolution: At low field speed with modest relative wind, air drag is normally a comparatively minor demand. Traction and implement/soil work, stability, cooling, visibility and practical equipment access generally govern the tractor's form more strongly than drag reduction.
conventionsAndLimits: Air drag is not asserted to be zero.
This is a design-priority judgment for the stipulated ordinary low-speed field conditions.
High-speed travel or strong wind can change priorities and is not proof for this case.
